contentHtml:
The Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) has signed a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Xiaohongshu. Image courtesy: DET

Marking the brand’s first strategic partnership in the Middle East. This major agreement strengthens Dubai’s ‘China Ready’ strategy,

Press Release

Through this inaugural regional partnership, Dubai and Xiaohongshu will collaborate to showcase the city’s diverse offerings in innovative ways, deepen connections with Chinese consumers, and inspire lasting engagement with Dubai.

Dubai, United Arab Emirates – The Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) has signed a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Xiaohongshu, also known as rednote, one of China’s leading lifestyle and social commerce platforms, marking the brand’s first strategic partnership in the Middle East. This major agreement strengthens Dubai’s ‘China Ready’ strategy, while creating new opportunities to reach wider global audiences through Xiaohongshu’s trusted audience ecosystem, further supporting Dubai’s ambition to consolidate its position as the best city in the world to visit, live and work in.

With hundreds of millions of users and a growing influence in China and across the globe, Xiaohongshu has evolved beyond a social media platform into a trusted discovery and lifestyle-sharing hub, where users share peer-led “notes” combining reviews, travel guides, photos and short-form video, making it a powerful space for authentic storytelling and inspiration. Its mission to “inspire lives” resonates deeply with Dubai’s character as a global hub of possibilities, where people from nearly 200 nationalities come together to discover, connect and explore.

Under the MoU, DET and Xiaohongshu will explore opportunities across destination promotion, content creation and storytelling, community engagement and creator initiatives, combining Xiaohongshu’s digital and community expertise with Dubai’s diverse destination offerings and track record for innovation in marketing. The framework will enable both parties to explore integrated opportunities supporting the full customer journey from awareness to deeper engagement through digital and real-world touchpoints, while building a richer base of genuine stories around Dubai.

The partnership reflects Dubai’s strategic focus on travel inspiration that is grounded in authentic experiences and trusted recommendations, strengthening relevance with a new generation of digitally connected travellers who plan and purchase through community-led platforms.

The signing ceremony was attended by Shahab Shayan, Regional Director, Asia Pacific at the Dubai Corporation for Tourism and Commerce Marketing (DCTCM), part of DET, on behalf of His Excellency Issam Kazim, CEO of DCTCM, and Dodo Kwong, Managing Director, Asia & Middle East, Global Business, Xiaohongshu, representing Tim Zhang, General Manager of Xiaohongshu’s Commercial Cross-Border and Internet Industry Group. Dodo Kwong was joined by Melanie Zhou, Market Lead of Middle East, Global Business, Xiaohongshu, and Simon Xu, Head of Overseas Partnership Management, Global Business, Xiaohongshu. The ceremony was witnessed by Hoor Al Khaja, Senior Vice President, International Operations at DCTCM.

Caption: Shahab Shayan, representing DET, and Dodo Kwong, representing Xiaohongshu, attended the signing ceremony of the strategic MoU.

Caption: Shahab Shayan (right), representing DET, and Dodo Kwong (left), representing Xiaohongshu, attended the signing ceremony of the strategic MoU, witnessed by Hoor Al Khaja (middle), Senior Vice President of International Operations at DCTCM.

Shahab Shayan, Regional Director, Asia Pacific at the Dubai Corporation for Tourism and Commerce Marketing (DCTCM) said: “We are delighted to be the first destination in the region to sign a strategic MoU with Xiaohongshu, bringing together our commitment to innovation in marketing and the power of co-creation. China continues to be a priority market for Dubai, supported by sustained engagement with consumers and the travel trade. The partnership aligns closely with Dubai’s wider strategic ambitions under the Dubai Economic Agenda, D33, supporting our efforts to further consolidate Dubai’s position as a leading global destination for business and leisure. With Xiaohongshu, we see an opportunity to go even further, by connecting Dubai’s destination offering with a new generation of travellers who are curious at heart, digitally savvy, experience-driven and inspired by trusted peer recommendations. Through this partnership we look forward to creating many more meaningful stories together, inspiring more people to discover Dubai and make it part of their own story.”

Dodo Kwong, Managing Director, Asia & Middle East, Global Business, Xiaohongshu said: “We are delighted to formalise our strategic partnership with the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism. This partnership represents an important milestone in Xiaohongshu’s long-term commitment to Dubai and our efforts to build a stronger ecosystem connecting Chinese consumers with the city. Travel is a natural starting point, but our ambition goes much further. Over time, we hope to extend Xiaohongshu’s ecosystem into other prominent sectors in Dubai, including retail, financial services, education, hospitality and lifestyle, helping businesses build stronger connections with Chinese consumers and supporting them not only as visitors, but also as people who return, stay longer and develop a lasting connection with Dubai.”

Dubai’s ‘China Ready’ approach is designed to make travel simpler and more familiar for Chinese visitors, including widely available Chinese digital payment options and expanded Mandarin-language support across visitor touchpoints. Looking ahead, the partnership marks a new chapter in Dubai’s engagement with global audiences. As Dubai continues to welcome visitors from around the world, the partnership will bring new momentum to inspiring more people to discover Dubai.

About the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET)

With the ultimate vision of making Dubai the world’s leading commercial centre, investment hub and tourism destination, the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) is mandated to support the Government in positioning the emirate as a major hub for global economy and tourism, and in boosting the city’s economic and tourism competitiveness indicators, in line with the goals of the Dubai Economic Agenda, D33, which aims to double the size of the emirate’s economy and further consolidate Dubai’s position as a leading global destination for business and leisure.

Under this remit, DET is driving efforts to further enhance Dubai’s diversified, innovative service-based economy to attract top global talent, deliver a world-class business environment and accelerate productivity growth. Additionally, DET is supporting Dubai’s vision to become the world’s best city to visit, live and work in by promoting its diverse destination proposition, unique lifestyle and outstanding quality of life, overall. 

DET is the principal authority for planning, supervising, developing and marketing Dubai’s business and tourism sectors. It is also responsible for licensing and classifying all types of businesses, including hotels, tour operators and travel agents. DET’s portfolio includes Dubai Economic Development Corporation (DEDC), Dubai Business Registration and Licensing Corporation (DBLC), Dubai Corporation for Consumer Protection and Fair Trade (DCCPFT), Dubai SME, Dubai Corporation for Tourism and Commerce Marketing (DCTCM), Dubai Festivals and Retail Establishment (DFRE) and Dubai College of Tourism (DCT).
